**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail J07 when launcher identity is absent**

When a report omits `launcher_identity` or supplies `null`, this branch silently skips the new identity gate, so all remaining J07 checks can pass without proving that the launcher is the expected shebang process. This also preserves old probe reports through the schema and `serde(default)` fallback; treat absent identity as a failure and make the contract breaking rather than bypassing the check.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L13-L13](https://github.com/jackin-project/jackin/blob/54bd572d2a9537ca3be2426e42427603c896bad2/AGENTS.md#L13-L13)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:64` still gates the whole identity block on `if let Some(identity) = &facts.launcher_identity`, so an absent/null `launcher_identity` still passes J07. This matches the signed contract: the sentinel probe emits `launcher_identity=null` whenever the launcher is not a shebang script or the cross-check fails (jackin-sentinel `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:2294-2296`), and `rewrite/probe-schema.json:818-826` keeps the field nullable for exactly that reason. Making absence a failure is a cross-repo contract change against jackin-sentinel#160 and is left to the author/operator. Not resolved.

Fixed and pushed in fb1ec5ee4. `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:90-95`: `identity_problems` now fails J07 when `launcher_identity` is absent or null (`"the probe report lacks the launcher identity facts"`) instead of gating the identity block on `if let Some(...)` and silently skipping it. No schema change was needed or made: `rewrite/probe-schema.json` `$defs/LauncherIdentity` keeps `launcher_identity` optional/nullable exactly as jackin-sentinel PR #160 emits it (null when the launcher is not a shebang script), but the J07 judge now treats absence as a failure, so old probe reports can no longer pass as if the launcher identity had been proven.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:85` `absent_or_null_launcher_identity_facts_are_rejected` (absent key and explicit null) — red against the old silent skip (`got []`), green after the fix. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 285/285, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` all green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require and compare launcher start-time evidence**

For the raw `/proc/PID/stat` evidence, zero-based `nth(2)` reads field 3—the process state—not field 22's start time, and the entire comparison is skipped when `stat_pre` is null. Two unrelated processes commonly have the same state, such as `S`, so a replaced or PID-reused launcher can pass this purported pre-launch identity binding; require `stat_pre` and compare the parsed start-time field.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- After fmt/clippy the comparison is at `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:119-121` and still compares `split_whitespace().nth(2)` (process state) and is still skipped when `stat_pre` is null. Correcting the field index (start time is field 22) is a judging-semantic change outside the scope of this CI-gate fix. Not resolved.

Fixed and pushed in fb1ec5ee4. `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:59-65` (`stat_identity`) now reads the start time from field 22 of `/proc/PID/stat` (skipping the parenthesised comm, so `nth(2)` no longer reads field 3, the process state); `stat_pre` is required (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:153-156`, `"the launcher identity record lacks the pre-launch stat evidence"`) and its parsed start time is compared with the one in `stat_before` (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:173-179`). Present-but-unparseable snapshots are rejected too (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:165-172`).

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:172` `the_pre_launch_start_time_is_read_from_the_start_time_field` — equal state + different field-22 start time is rejected, different state + equal start time is accepted (the state field is no longer mistaken for the start time); `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:205` `a_missing_pre_launch_stat_is_rejected` — both red before, green after. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 285/285, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` all green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject a missing launcher comm value**

When `launcher_identity.comm` is null while `processes.main` exists, this conditional performs no validation, even though the schema explicitly permits that null value. A partial identity record can therefore pass without binding its recorded command name to the observed main process; reject a missing or empty `comm` before comparing it with `main.comm`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:98-104` still compares `comm` with `processes.main.comm` only when both are `Some`; a null `comm` is not rejected. Not resolved by this delivery.

Fixed and pushed in fb1ec5ee4. `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:143-150`: a null or empty `comm` is now rejected (`"the launcher identity record lacks the recorded command name"`) before the comparison runs, and a present `comm` must equal `processes.main.comm`. A partial identity record can no longer pass without binding its recorded command name to the observed main process.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:144` `a_null_or_empty_comm_is_rejected` (null, empty, and a mismatching name) — red before (`got []`), green after. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 285/285, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` all green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cross-check the executable against the resolved interpreter**

When a probe emits contradictory evidence such as `exe_matches_interpreter: true` while `exe` differs from `interpreter_resolved`, this code accepts it because it trusts the derived boolean and checks the two paths only for non-emptiness. A probe regression can therefore make J07 pass even though the recorded running executable identifies the wrong interpreter; compare the resolved paths directly or otherwise reject inconsistent records.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:65-69` still trusts `checks.exe_matches_interpreter` and only requires `exe` to be non-empty (`:92-93`); it does not compare `exe` with `interpreter_resolved`. Not resolved by this delivery.

Fixed and pushed in fb1ec5ee4. `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:124-129` now performs a real comparison of the physical paths: `exe` must equal `interpreter_resolved` as resolved paths (`same_physical_path`, `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:67-75`, canonicalises symlinks when both paths exist on disk) in addition to requiring the derived `exe_matches_interpreter` boolean, so contradictory records (`exe_matches_interpreter: true` with `exe` differing from `interpreter_resolved`) are rejected.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:162` `a_mismatched_exe_is_rejected_even_when_the_boolean_claims_a_match` — red before (only non-emptiness was checked), green after. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 285/285, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` all green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify that the launcher runs as the sandbox user**

When the launcher runs under an unexpected account, such as UID 0, a nonempty `uid` value still satisfies this check. J04 verifies the separately executed probe and host command are UID 1000, not the already-running main process, so J07 can pass while `jackin-start` itself is privileged; parse this field and require the expected sandbox UID.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:95-96` still only requires a non-empty `uid`; it does not parse the value or compare it with the expected sandbox UID. Not resolved by this delivery.

Fixed and pushed in fb1ec5ee4. `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:131-140`: the `uid` field is parsed and must equal the expected sandbox uid 1000 (`SANDBOX_UID`, `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:57` — the same account J04 verifies). A launcher running as uid 0 (or any other uid) is now detected (`"the launcher runs as uid {uid}, not the sandbox uid 1000"`), and a missing or unparseable uid is rejected instead of passing on non-emptiness.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:104` `a_wrong_sandbox_uid_is_rejected` (uid "0", "root", "", null) — red before (`"0"` passed the non-empty check), green after. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 285/285, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` all green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind launcher evidence to the selected main PID**

When more than one `jackin-start`-named process exists, `LauncherIdentity` can describe a different process from `facts.processes.main`: it carries no typed PID, and the judge compares only the command name. Matching names and internally consistent stat snapshots from a decoy can therefore pass while the host process and agent checks concern another PID; carry or parse the PID and start time from `stat_before` and require them to equal `main.pid` and `main.start_ticks`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `LauncherIdentity` is regrouped at `crates/xtask/src/e2e/probe.rs:484-512` (`LauncherIdentityChecks` + `LauncherArgvMatches`, flattened so the flat JSON of `rewrite/probe-schema.json` `$defs/LauncherIdentity` and of the sentinel output `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:519-525` is byte-identical), but it still carries no PID and `judge_agent` still binds only the comm. Adding a field would change the frozen cross-repo wire format. Not resolved.

Fixed and pushed in fb1ec5ee4 without a wire-format change. `LauncherIdentity` still carries no PID field: `rewrite/probe-schema.json` `$defs/LauncherIdentity` and the serde structs keep the field names and types the sentinel emits (jackin-sentinel probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:519-525), so the flat JSON stays byte-identical for PR #160. Instead the judge parses the pid and start time from the `stat_before` evidence (`stat_identity`, `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:59-65`) and requires them to equal `processes.main.pid` and `processes.main.start_ticks` (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:180-187`), binding the identity record to the observed main process. A decoy `jackin-start` record describing another pid, or a reused pid with another start time, is rejected.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:120` `a_stale_pid_or_start_time_is_rejected` — red before (only the comm was compared), green after. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 285/285, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` all green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify stability from the recorded stat snapshots**

When `stat_before` and `stat_after` identify different PIDs or start times but the report sets `stable: true`, this check accepts the contradictory evidence because the snapshots are only checked for non-emptiness. That lets a launcher replacement during sampling pass J07; parse the PID and start-time fields from both snapshots and compare them rather than trusting the derived boolean alone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Pushed fixes (2d17ddab3 cargo fmt, b7295bb4c clippy grouping, af906be3e schema-contract test) repair the CI gates only and do not change J07 judging semantics, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- After fmt/clippy the check is at `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:126-128` and still trusts the derived `checks.stable` boolean; `stat_before`/`stat_after` are only required non-empty (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:105-116`). Deriving stability from the parsed snapshots is a judging-semantic change outside the scope of this CI-gate fix. Not resolved.

Fixed and pushed in fb1ec5ee4. Stability is now derived from the stat evidence: `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:189-193` parses the pid and start-time fields from `stat_before` and `stat_after` and rejects when they describe different processes (`"the launcher stat snapshots describe different processes"`), so `stable: true` with contradictory snapshots no longer passes. The derived `checks.stable` flag is still asserted as well (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:194-196`); it is just no longer trusted alone.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:213` `stability_is_derived_from_the_stat_snapshots` (stat_after with another pid and start time while `stable: true`) — red before (snapshots were only checked for non-emptiness), green after. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 285/285, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` all green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve executable paths inside the sandbox**

In the OpenShell J07 run, both paths describe the sandbox filesystem, but `std::fs::canonicalize` resolves them on the host running xtask. If the host aliases two paths that are distinct inside the role image, contradictory launcher evidence is accepted; conversely, sandbox aliases absent on the host are rejected. Compare already-resolved evidence directly or perform the resolution through the sandbox rather than using the host filesystem.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed in `9b023c8dc`.

The judge no longer resolves the recorded paths on the host that runs xtask. `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:112-119` now compares the recorded `exe` with the recorded `interpreter_resolved` directly, and the `same_physical_path` helper (the `std::fs::canonicalize` call) is deleted, so no host filesystem is consulted at all.

Why the direct comparison is the sandbox comparison: both recorded values are already resolved inside the sandbox, so the comparison is made on the sandbox filesystem by construction. The probe records the executable from the sandbox's own `/proc/<pid>/exe` (jackin-sentinel PR #160, `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:469` `record_exe=$(readlink "/proc/$record_pid/exe" 2>/dev/null)`) and resolves the interpreter with the in-sandbox `physical_path` helper (`probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:364-380`, used at `:468` `record_resolved=$(physical_path "$record_interpreter")`). The probe itself compares the two inside the sandbox (`:477-478` `record_exe_path=$(physical_path "$record_exe")` / `[ "$record_exe_path" = "$record_resolved" ] || return 1`). The kernel path and `physical_path` resolve the same way, so the recorded strings are equal exactly when the two sandbox paths are the same file.

The host resolution could only ever add or remove decisions, never add evidence: it accepted two distinct sandbox paths that the host aliases to one file, and it rejected a sandbox alias the host does not know. The new comparison is stricter in the aliasing case and identical in every other case, so no assertion is weakened.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:228` `the_launcher_paths_are_compared_without_the_host_filesystem` — a temp directory holds a symlink alias that the host resolves to the same inode as the real file; the judge rejects the record — red before (the host canonicalization accepted it), green after.

The wire format is unchanged: `rewrite/probe-schema.json` `$defs/LauncherIdentity` and the serde structs in `crates/xtask/src/e2e/probe.rs` are untouched, so the flat JSON stays byte-identical for the sentinel contract of PR #160.

Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 287/287, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare the pre-launch PID as well**

When `stat_pre` describes a different process created in the same clock tick as `stat_before`, this comparison accepts it because it discards both parsed PIDs and compares only `start_ticks`, which are not globally unique. The pre-launch snapshot is intended to bind the same process across `exec`, so compare the complete `(pid, start_ticks)` tuples.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed in `9b023c8dc`.

`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:164-170` now compares the complete `(pid, start time)` tuples of the pre-launch and the pre-restart snapshot instead of the start time alone, so a snapshot of another process created in the same clock tick no longer passes. The pid is not discarded any more.

The legitimate record stays valid: the pre-launch snapshot and the later snapshot are the stat of the same launcher pid (jackin-sentinel PR #160, `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:2285` `launcher_stat_pre=$(proc_stat "$launcher_pid")` and `:481` `record_before=$(proc_stat "$record_pid")` for that same pid), and `exec` keeps the pid and the start time, so the tuples are equal.

Contract test: `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:213` `a_pre_launch_snapshot_from_another_pid_is_rejected` — a `stat_pre` that describes pid 999 with the same start time is rejected — red before (only the start time was compared), green after. The existing `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:172` `the_pre_launch_start_time_is_read_from_the_start_time_field` still proves that the process state is not mistaken for the start time: a different state with the same pid and start time is accepted.

Gates: `cargo nextest run -p jackin-xtask` 287/287, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackin-xtask --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo xtask ci --only comments,layers,pins,containers,errors` green.

Resolving.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require launcher identity in the schema**

When an older probe omits `launcher_identity`, the final aggregate still accepts the report at the schema boundary because this field is added only under `properties`, while `FactsJ07.required` still ends at `agent_exec`; `identity_problems` then rejects the same report later. This preserves the legacy-report compatibility explicitly forbidden by the repository rules and makes an invalid producer contract masquerade as a well-formed J07 report. Fresh evidence relative to the earlier thread is that the final diff still does not add this field to `required`; require it here so the version mismatch fails at schema validation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L13-L13](https://github.com/jackin-project/jackin/blob/9b023c8dc3b0593d041d2724a501f6294ecc9290/AGENTS.md#L13-L13)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**Coordination checked first: the schema flip is not safe before jackin-sentinel#160 merges, so the field stays optional and nullable. Evidence below.**

**1. How the e2e obtains the probe — a local sentinel checkout, not a pinned ref and not a vendored copy**
- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/args.rs:18-22` — `--role DIR` is required and is a local path ("The sentinel role repository").
- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/setup.rs:118-137` — the role path is canonicalized as a local directory; `crates/xtask/src/e2e/setup.rs:263-266` — `jackin role add sentinel <role>` registers that local checkout as the role that builds the image.
- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j00.rs:129-133` — the e2e reads `<role>/probe/jackin-sentinel-probe` from that checkout and hashes it; `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j00.rs:176` together with `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j00.rs:87-89` (`judge_late`) require the in-image `/usr/local/bin/jackin-sentinel-probe` digest to equal that local file's digest ("the installed probe digest differs from the role's probe file"). The probe that actually runs is therefore exactly the file in the operator's local jackin-sentinel checkout, whatever ref is checked out there — `main` by default. No ref is pinned in jackin and no copy is vendored.
- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/run.rs:29` and `:361-380` — that binary is executed in the sandbox and its stdout is parsed by `parse_probe` → `ProbeReport::parse`.

**2. The e2e does validate every probe report against `rewrite/probe-schema.json`**
- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/probe.rs:18` embeds the schema; `:116-143` (`deeper`) re-validates each step's facts against `#/$defs/Facts{step}`; `:145-161` (`validate`) runs the whole report through the validator; `:166-179` (`ProbeReport::parse`) calls `validate` before deserializing, so a violation is `ProbeError::Schema` ("the probe output breaks probe-schema.json") and fails the step.

**3. The sentinel main probe does not emit the field**
- jackin-sentinel `main` `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:2055-2088` — `step_J07` seals the facts as `{processes: $p[0], agent_exec: $x[0]}` only; `launcher_identity` occurs nowhere in main's probe.
- The field first appears in the open sentinel PR #160 (`fix/probe-interpreter-identity`, head `9b0a4af0`): `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:460-527` (`proc_launcher_identity_record`, the 14 flat fields at `:526-528`), `:2292-2294` and `:2324-2326` — the key is always emitted, `null` when the launcher identity cannot be recorded.

**4. So requiring the key now would break the e2e against the current sentinel main**
- With `launcher_identity` in `$defs/FactsJ07.required` (`rewrite/probe-schema.json:807-810`), a sentinel-main J07 report carries no such key, so `validate` (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/probe.rs:145-161`) rejects it and the J07 probe invocation fails with "the probe output breaks probe-schema.json" — the same failure class recorded for a probe/schema mismatch in `rewrite/evidence/A14-t09-reproof.md:20`.
- It is also a breaking change to the frozen wire contract that jackin cannot make alone: `rewrite/probe-schema.json` `properties.schema` is `{"const": 3, "description": "The version of this contract. A breaking change raises it."}`, and both sentinel main (`probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:3474`) and PR #160 (`:3747`) still emit `schema: 3`. A new mandatory key inside a schema-3 document must raise the const to 4 in lockstep with the sentinel probe, which is not possible from this branch.
- For completeness: the e2e already fails against sentinel main today — at the judge (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:82-85`), not at the schema — because main's probe never emits the identity. The flip would only move that failure from the judge to the schema validator; it would not make the run pass, and it would invalidate every other schema-3 producer.

**5. The security property already holds without the schema flip**
- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:80-85` — `identity_problems` fails the verdict with "the probe report lacks the launcher identity facts" when the identity is absent or `null`; it runs for every J07 verdict via `judge_agent` (`j07.rs:197`, called at `j07.rs:332`).
- `crates/xtask/tests/e2e/k_identity.rs:84-101` — the contract test proves that a payload without the key and a payload with `null` are both rejected, while `:78-82` proves the complete record passes.
